title: UAE Armed Forces Recruitment 2026: Joining Guide
metaDescription: UAE Armed Forces recruitment 2026: National Service rules, age 18-30, 11-month service, professional enlistment, eligibility, pay and how to apply.
headline: UAE Armed Forces Recruitment 2026: National Service and Careers

sections.title: National Service: Mandatory for Emirati Men
sections.content:
National Service, known in Arabic as Al Khidma Al Wataniya, is mandatory for medically fit Emirati men aged 18 to 30 under Federal Law No. 6 of 2014. Men who hold a high school certificate or higher serve 11 months, while those without a high school qualification serve three years. For Emirati women, service is optional for 11 months with guardian consent.

Service can be completed in the Armed Forces, the Ministry of Defense, the Ministry of Interior, the State Security Service or other designated institutions. Those who complete it gain priority for government and private-sector jobs, marriage grants, housing plots and scholarships.

sections.title: Who Can Join and What It Takes
sections.content:
National Service recruits must be UAE citizens, aged 18 to 30 for men and up to 35 for women, medically fit, and approved by the National and Reserve Service Committee. Professional enlistment in the Armed Forces is also primarily open to UAE nationals, generally aged 18 to 30, with at least a high school diploma for general soldier roles and a bachelor's degree or higher for officer ranks.

All applicants must pass a medical examination and background checks, meet height and weight standards, and complete the required fitness assessments. Technical and specialist roles, including engineering, cyber security and logistics, are a priority for the Ministry of Defense in 2026.

sections.title: Branches, Training and Career Benefits
sections.content:
The UAE Armed Forces include the Land Forces, Air Force and Naval Forces, all under the Ministry of Defense. Recruits train at military academies and training centres, learning weapons handling, fieldcraft, physical conditioning and their specialist trade, with officer cadets following a longer academic and leadership programme.

Military service in the UAE carries strong benefits: competitive tax-free salaries, free medical care, housing support and a clear promotion path from soldier to senior non-commissioned and commissioned ranks. Completing National Service is also a prerequisite for many government roles, including Abu Dhabi Police, which requires both the foundational and specialised service courses.

sections.title: How to Apply in 2026
sections.content:
Applications for professional roles are submitted through the Ministry of Defense recruitment portal, using UAE PASS for identity verification. Candidates create a profile with their personal details, education and National Service status, upload their documents, and are then contacted for medical checks, fitness tests and interviews.

For National Service itself, eligible citizens are notified and register within 30 days through the designated authorities. Apply only through official government channels: genuine UAE military recruitment never asks for application fees, and any person or website demanding payment is a scam.

faqs.q: Is National Service mandatory in the UAE?
faqs.a: Yes, National Service is mandatory for medically fit Emirati men aged 18 to 30 under Federal Law No. 6 of 2014. Men with a high school certificate serve 11 months, while those without one serve three years. For women, service is optional for 11 months and needs guardian consent.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not enlist for UAE National Service?
faqs.a: Citizens who fail to enlist without a valid reason by age 29 face a jail term of one month to one year, a fine of AED 10,000 to 50,000, or both, and must still complete the service even after passing the age limit. Medical and other genuine exemptions are decided under the executive regulations.

faqs.q: Can expatriates join the UAE Armed Forces?
faqs.a: Combat and uniformed roles are reserved for UAE nationals. Expatriates with high-level technical expertise can sometimes work in defence consultancy or civilian technical specialist posts, usually through private contractors rather than direct enlistment in the Armed Forces, and they must hold valid UAE residency and work permits.

faqs.q: How do I apply for UAE Armed Forces recruitment?
faqs.a: Apply through the official Ministry of Defense recruitment portal using UAE PASS, with your national ID, education certificates and National Service status. After registration you will be called for medical checks, fitness tests and interviews. Never pay anyone for recruitment, as official applications are free.
